name: Underground Resistance
hook: A second-generation Detroit collective who ran techno as a political project, in ski masks, against major labels and the artists who signed to them.
blurb: Underground Resistance was founded in 1989 by Mike Banks, Jeff Mills and Robert Hood. They rejected the major-label deals some of the first Detroit techno artists, the Belleville Three generation, had begun to accept, and tied that stand to the same economic collapse of Detroit in the Reagan years that the earlier scene had made central to its identity. They performed and released records anonymously, in masks and combat gear, treating techno as a tool for political and economic independence rather than a genre to be sold off. The group was both a production team and an independent label, and refused distribution deals that would hand over control of their recordings, a direct answer to the label stories that run through this map.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A harsh, minimal statement of the militant, anti-commercial second wave of Detroit techno.
